subject: Hosted API — annual commit increase & tiered rate re-balance
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Porter <sarah.porter@orbitalcommerce.com>
Cc: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@orbitalcommerce.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API — annual commit increase & tiered rate re-balance

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I attached a concise amendment that annualizes your hosted API commit and introduces a small tiered rate re-balance to smooth month-to-month overage exposure. High-level summary: 

- Current monthly committed token spend: 1.2M tokens
- Proposal: Annualized commit equivalent to 1.5M tokens/month (12-month term)
- Add a 15% burst pool (short-term capacity for traffic spikes) with a soft overage cap that gradually ramps down during Q4
- Rate re-balance: marginal per-token rates adjusted across tiers to reflect predictable unit economics

Why we recommend this: it reduces your per-token unit price by ~18% while keeping headroom for seasonal spikes without surprise invoices. It also lets us reserve dedicated capacity during your peak windows to preserve latency SLOs.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You review the attached amendment draft (PDF)
2) If agreed, I’ll loop in Legal for a quick redline and Procurement for PO/terms
3) We can turn DocuSign within 48 hours once we agree on the overage handling

Questions I already know will come up: latency guarantees during burst usage and how overage is billed — I’ve noted a short explainer in page 2 of the attachment.

Would you be able to confirm a target effective date? We can backdate to 7/1 if you want the annualization tied to your fiscal quarter.

Best,
Rachel

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0196

Attachment: 20270627-proposed-amendment.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

From: Sarah Porter <sarah.porter@orbitalcommerce.com>

Date: 2027-06-27T10:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — annual commit increase & tiered rate re-balance

Rachel —

Appreciate the summary and the PDF. A couple quick questions from our side before we loop Procurement fully in: 

1) For the 15% burst pool, what controls are available if we see sustained usage at burst levels? Does it drop into the committed bucket or bill as overage?
2) Latency SLO: we rely on tail latency during checkout flows — can you confirm whether reserving capacity guarantees p95 p99 under the proposed commit?
3) Do you have a clean CSV of the pricing model so we can run it through forecast?

If those are okay, Procurement will ask for the redline but we prefer a single DocuSign for efficiency. Target effective date: 2027-07-01 ideally.

Thanks,
Sarah

Sarah Porter
Director, Platform Engineering — Orbital Commerce
sarah.porter@orbitalcommerce.com

Rachel / Karthik —

I ran a quick simulation (see attached XLSX). Summary: reserving the burst as a bounded pool with explicit autoscale headroom keeps the tail latency within existing SLOs for 92% of simulated peak events. For the remaining 8% — sustained >60s of peak traffic — we recommend an explicit fallback policy (route non-critical batch requests to a lower-cost model variant) rather than scaling indefinitely.

Concretely: 
- Option A (recommended): 15% burst pool + model fallback policy for non-essential traffic; max dedicated nodes increased by 10% during peak windows.
- Option B (conservative): convert burst to a temporary committed uplift for the quarterly peak months only (~20% uplift for Q4) — this lowers risk but increases committed spend.

I've attached batching-impact-analysis.xlsx with the simulation and charts. Happy to walk through numbers in a short call.

Marissa

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API — pricing model v2 and DocuSign path

Rachel —

Attached is pricing model v2 (CSV). High-level proposal: two-step commercial path to make it palatable to Procurement and Ops: 

1) Immediate: annualize to 1.5M committed tokens/month; apply new tiered per-token rates that reduce unit price by ~18% compared to their current band.
2) Operational guardrail: 15% burst pool billed at a slightly higher marginal rate but with a monthly cap; if burst usage exceeds cap more than twice in a rolling 6-month window, we convert the burst into a temporary quarter-commit uplift and credit them for the difference at renewal.

For DocuSign: I can push the amendment to DocuSign once Legal gives the greenlight on the language (Ben — can you confirm?) — target turnaround: 48 hours after redline acceptance.

Link to pricing CSV: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Orbital_Commit_Workbook (sheet: pricing_v2)

Karthik
